panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Image clearly shows the cystic structure arising from the bladder wall, consistent with a congenital bladder diverticulum. b: Image shows the internal morphology of the diverticulum, specifically the narrow neck, which is a characteristic feature. c: This panel shows the internal cavity structure of the diverticulum during endoscopic examination. d: Image provides a detailed view of the internal mucosal lining of the bladder diverticulum.

(d) Detailed view of the mucosal surface within the diverticulum.
in_text_mentions: Cystoscopy demonstrated a normal urethra, bladder neck, and orthotopic right ureteric orifice. A large diverticulum arising from the left posterolateral bladder wall with a narrow neck was identified (Fig. 3a–d). The left ureteric orifice was not visualized within the native bladder, supporting ureteric insertion into the diverticulum.

plate_findings.evidence: identification of a contrast-filled structure located to the left and posterior to the bladder

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Micturating cystourethrogram shows an abnormal contrast-filled structure posterior to the bladder, suggestive of a bladder diverticulum. B: VCUG shows the structure enlarging and demonstrating a ureteric orifice arising from its superior aspect, consistent with complex congenital diverticulum. C: VCUG demonstrates contrast reflux reaching the left kidney, related to the visualization of the diverticular structure in the bladder.
panels.attribution_text: Costa et al. Laparoscopic diverticulectomy and ureteric reimplantation for congenital bladder diverticulum.. Journal of surgical case reports 2026. doi:10.1093/jscr/rjag637. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Micturating cystourethrogram demonstrating initial normal bladder filling (a), followed by identification of a contrast-filled structure located to the left and posterior to the bladder (a). The structure communicates with the bladder and enlarges during voiding (b). During the voiding phase, a ureter is visualized arising from the superior aspect of this structure, with contrast reflux extending to the left kidney (b, c). No vesicoureteric reflux is observed on the right side. These findings are indeterminate, with differential considerations including focal dilatation of the distal left ureter and a large bladder diverticulum with ureteric insertion.

plate_findings.evidence: Cystic structure consistent with a bladder diverticulum is identified arising from the left posteroinferior aspect of the bladder

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Panel (a) is a diagnostic ultrasound showing the characteristic cystic diverticulum associated with the target disease, confirming the morphological suspicion of a Hutch diverticulum. b: Panel (b) provides clinical context for the disease, demonstrating significant post-void residual volume (137 ml), which is common in bladder outlet obstruction related to large bladder issues or diverticula. c: Panel (c) shows Color Doppler evidence (urinary jets) of communication between the diverticulum and the bladder lumen, a key feature of the pathophysiology of this diverticulum.
panels.attribution_text: Costa et al. Laparoscopic diverticulectomy and ureteric reimplantation for congenital bladder diverticulum.. Journal of surgical case reports 2026. doi:10.1093/jscr/rjag637. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound of the urinary tract demonstrating a thin-walled urinary bladder with a pre-void volume of 272 ml (a) and a significant post-void residual volume of 137 ml (b). A cystic structure consistent with a bladder diverticulum is identified arising from the left posteroinferior aspect of the bladder, measuring 29 × 27 mm, with associated urothelial thickening. Colour Doppler demonstrates urinary jets passing from the diverticulum into the bladder lumen.
